title: Surgery Residency Scheduling | Compliance Built In
description: Surgery residency scheduling is complex. Our managed service delivers optimized, ACGME-compliant block, call, and clinic schedules directly to your inbox.
h1: Surgery Residency Scheduling Without The Burden
paragraph: Send us your surgery program's rules and we build the schedule to the ACGME requirements and send it back finished.

cta.title: Stop Building Surgery Schedules From Scratch
cta.description: Join the 30+ departments across 20+ hospitals and practices that already trust Scheduling Wizard with their residency scheduling. Finished schedules in your format, with redrafts through the year included.

faq.answer: ACGME compliance is built into the schedule as it is created, not checked manually afterward. Our team has subspecialty-specific ACGME duty hour rules built in, including the 80-hour weekly limit, eight hours off between duty periods between shifts, and the 24-hour hard cap. For surgical programs specifically, our team accounts for the specific call and trauma coverage rules that are unique to surgery. The rules are applied before the schedule reaches your program.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard ensure ACGME compliance for surgery residency schedules?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard generates complete Block, Call, Clinic, and Attending schedules for surgical residency and fellowship programs. All four schedule types are optimized simultaneously, so a change in one automatically propagates across the others. The finished schedules are delivered as Excel spreadsheets that programs can upload directly to their existing publishing platform.
faq.question: What types of schedules does Scheduling Wizard generate for surgery programs?

faq.answer: Fairness is algorithmically optimized, not estimated. Our team distributes call, weekend, and holiday burden equitably across all residents in a surgical program while simultaneously respecting ACGME duty hour limits and individual rules. This eliminates the manual back-and-forth and "why do I have more weekend call?" disputes that are common with spreadsheet-based scheduling.
faq.question: How is surgery residency call scheduling made fair across all residents?

faq.answer: Institutional scheduling knowledge persists with Scheduling Wizard across annual chief rotations. Your program's rule configurations, rules, and preferences are retained year over year. Incoming chief residents inherit a fully operational, optimized system instead of starting from a blank spreadsheet, which eliminates the steep annual learning curve that burdens most surgical programs.
faq.question: What happens when a new chief resident takes over the surgery program?

faq.answer: No, and many surgery programs do exactly that. Scheduling Wizard handles the build, producing finished schedules built to the ACGME requirements as Excel or Google Sheets files. Programs then upload them to whatever platform they already publish on.
faq.question: Does Scheduling Wizard replace the platform we use now for surgery programs?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard primarily works with chief residents, program directors, and program coordinators at surgical residency and fellowship programs. Chief residents benefit most from the managed service model since they do not need to learn scheduling software. Program directors benefit from institutional continuity across chief rotations. Program coordinators benefit from conflict detection and revision handling throughout the academic year.
faq.question: Who at a surgery residency program typically works with Scheduling Wizard?

faq.answer: No. Scheduling Wizard focuses on building and optimizing your schedule, the output is delivered as a ready-to-use Excel file that your program can upload directly to whatever platform you already use. Many Scheduling Wizard clients continue using the platform they already have to publish the schedule day-to-day while Scheduling Wizard handles all schedule creation and optimization.
faq.question: Do we need to replace the scheduling tools we already use?

faq.answer: The process has three steps. First, your program submits its scheduling rules, rotation requirements, ACGME rules, resident preferences, call coverage targets, and any site-specific rules. Second, our team builds a compliant, finished schedule. Third, you receive a finished Excel file ready to review and publish. No software to learn, no platform to onboard.
